institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Relevant courses at the university, The city and surrounding area.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed my exchange a lot!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I recieved my letter of acceptance very late, and didnt get any information before that.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a very informative and nice intro days where we go a lot of information and could ask the question we had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and had a friend who had a friend who knew a place which i got. But there are a lot of housing website where you can find housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed being closer to the big forest. There were already people living there so most kitchen supplies were allready there, and kknow someone who lived on campus who had to buy everything

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was a bit messy, i wasnt allowed for the courses i originally applied for, so i had to find all new courses. I found it hard to find courses where the schedule didnt overlap, and it wasnt possible to search by time/schedule. 
But a good thing, you could register for as much courses as you want and then delete the ones you didnt want before a certain deadline

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Se above

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: you could ask the course responsible for help, or go to the international house at the university

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: not very succesful for the original courses, but i ended up finding som nice courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: dont worry to much about it, you might not get the courses you planned for but there are so many courses so you will find something

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses and teachers were really good and some were less, but thats how its always is i guess

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: the same, mix of lectures, exercises, group projects, discussions

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Participatory design 
advance tools for performance engineering
Patenting and Commercialization of Biotech and Medtech Inventions
Sustainable system engineering

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sustainable system engineering, was a fun course with a lot of international students, the course was based on group work, which i found nice so you didnt just sat by yourself at lectures. 
 I really enjoyed advance tools for performance engineering, before i only did smaller porgramming projects, but in this course  did some bigger systems and got familiar with programming. It was a lot of work but i learned a lot!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I knew food and alcohol is expensive, but fresh vegetables and fruit and cheese were even more expensive than i thought 
I think the prices when going out to eat was cheaper than expected it was similar or somtimes cheaper than in copenhagen

Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing, you could join any sportsteam you can imagine and there was so many activites to do

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: sports, craft-cafes, talks, special courses, cabin rental etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sport team and go to studentsamfunnet.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: go to bymarka for skiing and hiking, take trips around the area and explore, go on a cabin trip

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy, i think it is quite similar to the danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just do it, they also want to talk.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: the prices :(

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the way they use and appreciate the outdoors

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: bring skiing clothes, enjoy the outdoors and go to loftet if you want to meet other students
